texts: Restrictive physiology of the right ventricle after tetralogy repair is treated with all of the above: E.

A stiff, poorly filling right ventricle needs a high preload, so volume is given, and positive airway pressure, which impedes venous return and raises the afterload of the right ventricle, is kept to a minimum or replaced by spontaneous breathing.
Effusions and ascites are drained, as they raise intrathoracic and abdominal pressure, and inotropes, which raise heart rate and stiffen filling further, are avoided where possible.
In the picture, Chopper lets the hotel breathe on its own, pours water in, mops the puddles and keeps the fireworks away.
Memory hook: a stiff blue room needs gentle breath, more water, dry puddles and no fireworks.
